question: How does the prediction objective shape the composite query-key matrix of self-attention, and can the resulting structure improve Transformer initialization?

key_findings.claim: The gradient update of the composite query-key matrix can be written as a sum of token-embedding outer products whose row and column effects depend differently on whether a token is context or prediction target.
key_findings.evidence: Propositions 2.1 and 2.2 derive the implicit update for WqWk-transpose and separate contributions by context and target roles. Under stated distributional and error-symmetry assumptions, theorems then predict column dominance for causal objectives and approximate symmetric updates for bidirectional objectives.

key_findings.claim: Encoder-only pretrained models have more symmetric composite query-key matrices, while decoder-only models show greater row-column directionality across text, vision, and audio families.
key_findings.evidence: Symmetry and directionality scores are evaluated over BERT/ModernBERT, GPT, LLaMA, Mistral, T5, and additional modality models. Controlled encoder-versus-decoder training on Jigsaw, Wikipedia, and RedPajama reproduces the divergence over time and shows especially directional later decoder layers.

key_findings.claim: Initializing encoder self-attention so the composite query-key matrix is symmetric speeds convergence in the tested language-model settings.
key_findings.evidence: Across 4-, 12-, and 24-layer encoders, symmetric initialization reaches the ordinary model's terminal loss up to 75%, 35%, and 44% sooner, respectively, and usually lowers final loss. The matrices lose perfect symmetry during training but converge to more symmetric states than random initialization.

method.core_idea: Analyze self-attention through the single bilinear-form matrix WqWk-transpose and derive how causal versus bidirectional token roles accumulate structural updates.
method.mechanism: The paper derives rank-one implicit gradient contributions, formalizes symmetry and row-column directionality scores, surveys pretrained matrices across architectures/modalities, tracks those scores during controlled training, and initializes Wq and Wk jointly to impose a symmetric product for encoder models.
assumptions: Token embeddings and prediction errors satisfy the alignment and approximate symmetry assumptions used in the theorems.
The composite matrix is the appropriate unit even though Wq and Wk are separately parameterized and multihead attention includes values and softmax.
Matrix symmetry and directionality scores correspond to useful information-processing structure.

techniques.role: Treats attention logits as a learned bilinear form rather than separate query and key factors.
Links context/target asymmetry to row and column structure in parameter updates.
Imposes the predicted encoder prior at initialization to accelerate training.

evaluations.setting: Pretrained encoder, decoder, and encoder-decoder Transformers across text, vision, and audio
evaluations.metric: median query-key symmetry and directionality scores
evaluations.result: Encoder-only models consistently score as more symmetric and decoder-only models as more directional.
evaluations.baseline: Random matrices and model families trained under other objective types.

evaluations.setting: 4-, 12-, and 24-layer encoder pretraining on Jigsaw, Wikipedia, and RedPajama
evaluations.metric: terminal loss and epochs to the ordinary initialization's terminal loss
evaluations.result: Symmetric initialization is reported up to 75% faster for 4 layers, 35% for 12 layers, and 44% for 24 layers, with lower final loss in most configurations.
evaluations.baseline: Independent random query and key initialization.

limitations: The theoretical directionality result relies on simplified token-frequency, embedding, and error-signal assumptions.
The scalar scores summarize matrices but do not establish that individual high-norm columns encode the predicted semantics.
Initialization experiments target encoder-only language models and do not test whether an analogous causal prior helps decoders.
Reviewer inference: architecture, masking, positional encoding, and data differ across pretrained families, so controlled training is more probative than the broad model survey.
failure_modes: Rotations or reparameterizations of query/key factors change apparent structure without changing attention logits.
Symmetric initialization constrains optimization toward a poor solution when the task itself is asymmetric.
Directionality scores are dominated by a few norm outliers unrelated to useful token-order computation.
reusable_insights: Analyze parameter products that directly determine a computation, not arbitrary nonidentifiable factors.
Objective-induced asymmetries can be converted into structured initialization hypotheses.
Pretrained-weight observations should be followed by controlled from-scratch trajectory tests.
open_questions: Can direction-aware initialization improve causal decoders without harming stability or expressivity?
Which linguistic or positional features occupy the high-norm columns predicted by the theory?
Do the scores predict model behavior after controlling for architecture, scale, and data?

competitive_landscape.title: Mimetic Initialization of Self-Attention Layers
competitive_landscape.difference: Mimetic initialization observes identity-like query-key products and negative-identity value-output products in pretrained vision Transformers and hard-codes those priors. This paper derives broader objective-dependent symmetry/directionality predictions and validates symmetric initialization mainly for language encoders.

competitive_landscape.title: What Does BERT Look At? An Analysis of BERT's Attention
competitive_landscape.difference: Clark et al. interpret learned attention patterns and their linguistic relations in BERT activations. This paper studies the parameter-space bilinear form, derives its update structure, and compares objectives rather than annotating head attention maps.

competitive_landscape.title: A phase transition between positional and semantic learning in a solvable model of dot-product attention
competitive_landscape.difference: That work analyzes a solvable dot-product-attention model and a transition between positional and semantic solutions. This paper derives row/column updates for standard self-attention and tests structural signatures across real pretrained families.

novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference after comparison: the distinctive contribution is an objective-sensitive derivation for the composite query-key matrix, followed by unusually broad matrix audits and a causal initialization test. It advances beyond descriptive attention maps, though its theoretical assumptions and semantic interpretation remain only partially tested.
reviewer_notes: Main derivations, appendical assumptions/proofs, pretrained surveys, controlled trajectories, initialization table, and discussion were reviewed. Competitor primary records were checked on 2026-08-23.
